milestones.label: Gödel and Herbrand formalise general recursive functions
milestones.description: Gödel, with Herbrand, gave a formal class of general recursive functions, an early candidate for computability.

evidence.claim: Gödel with Herbrand formalised general recursive functions in 1933

milestones.note: Lecture-based precursor; no public paper was checked, so this is a note, not a priority claim.

milestones.label: Church's lambda-definability thesis
milestones.work: Church, An Unsolvable Problem of Elementary Number Theory, American Journal of Mathematics 58 (1936) 345-363
milestones.description: Church proposed that effectively calculable functions are exactly the lambda-definable (general recursive) functions.

milestones.note: Wikipedia notes the abstract was received in 1935; the 1936 publication year governs.

milestones.label: Post's finite combinatory processes
milestones.work: Post, Finite combinatory processes - formulation I, Journal of Symbolic Logic 1 (1936) 103-105
milestones.description: Post gave an independent formulation of finite combinatory processes as a model of mechanical procedure.

milestones.label: Turing machines applied to the Entscheidungsproblem
milestones.work: Turing, On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem, Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (2) 42 (1937) 230-265
milestones.description: Turing defined an abstract machine and a universal machine and used them to show the Entscheidungsproblem has no solution.

evidence.claim: Turing, On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem, Proc. London Math. Soc. (2) 42 (1937) 230-265
Turing's 1936 paper established a universal Turing machine and his application to computing

milestones.note: The same paper also gives the machine model; it is listed once, under first_application, because the model is only used here as the application. The Church-Turing priority debate is noted in the source text.

canonicalName: Computational group theory: computers enter group theory

evidence.source: MacTutor, History of Computational Group Theory

milestones.note: Unpublished report: precursor only.
